2. Three sets of plaintiff-respondents, plaintiff Nos. 1.-11, plaintiff No. 12 and plaintiff No.13 filed the suit for a declaration of title in respect of 48 acres, .09 acres and .1876 acres of land respectively of CS plot No.128, now SA plot No. 1357 at mouza Nutun Paltan Line, JL No. 250, PS. Lalbagh, District Dhaka contending, inter alia, that the suit land is their ancestral property consisting of homestead and kutcha houses where they reside with their family members on payment of rent to and upon obtaining rent receipts from the Dhaka Collectorate peacefully, quietly and without any interference or obstruction either from the Government or from any other person or persons. Besides the plaintiffs and their family members, many other destitute persons have been residing on the same plot for a long time in kutcha huts on payment of rent to the plaintiffs. Defendant No. 2, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka has been unlawfully issuing notices to the plaintiffs since 1962 under Government Lands and Buildings (Recovery of possession) Act, 1953 asking them to vacate the suit land on pain of forcible eviction. The plaintiffs' representations to the concerned authorities were of no avail and defendant No. 2 again issued scores of notices on the inhabitants of the suit land directing them to quit and vacate the same by the 16th June, 1964 in default of which they would be evicted by force. The plaintiffs filed the suit in 1964 asserting that they are the hereditary owners of the suit land and had obtained tenancy right therein under the Government. They paid rent to the Government upto 1962 where after the staffs of the Acquired Estate refused to accept the same. 

 15. There is absolutely no averment in the plaint as to the kind of land that the plaintiffs took possession of as far back as in 1936. Rule 209 of the Bengal Government Estates Manual, 1932 provided as follows, 

 "Town Khas Mahal lands consist of urban lands not used or likely to be used for agricultural purposes. They are governed by the Transfer of Property Act and not by the Bengal Tenancy Act except where lands though used for non-agricultural purposes now were originally leased to raiyat who had subsequently acquired occupancy rights. Agricultural lands within a municipal area, leased for cultivation, are not included within town khas mahals land." 

 17. Except for producing some rent-receipts Exts. 1(e) to 1(h) from 1936 to 1942 the plaintiffs have failed to produce any tangible evidence of settlement of suit land with them by the Government by following any of the procedure laid down in the said Manual 1932. It must be borne in mind that the plaintiffs were not claiming tenancy under a private landlord but under the Government, not under the Bengal Tenancy Act or the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act but by virtue of settlements from the khas Mahal Department. In the absence of any record of settlement by way of observing any formalities provided in the different Rules of the said Manual, 1932, the plaintiffs cannot be given a declaration of title over the suit land merely on production of collateral evidence. The High Court Division committed an error of law in this regard because even on the finding of formal proof of the rent-receipts and the S.A. khatians the legal conclusion from the so-called proved facts does not follow. The rent-receipts after 1942 are coming from 1958 (Ext. 1(c) and there is no explanation what happened to the intervening years from 1943 to 1957.
